summary: Configured node1 so only root and opsadmin may schedule cron jobs. The policy and cron service persisted across a verified node restart; the OS release and kernel were unchanged.
actions_performed: Created the opsadmin account with a home directory and Bash shell.
Created /etc/cron.allow containing exactly root and opsadmin, owned by root:root with mode 0644.
Verified root and opsadmin are accepted by crontab while nobody is denied.
Safely restarted node1 and verified recovery and persistence.

evidence.requirement: Only root and opsadmin can schedule cron jobs
evidence.summary: The policy contains exactly root and opsadmin. Functional crontab checks allow both accounts and deny nobody, before and after restart.

evidence.requirement: Keep the installed OS release and kernel
evidence.summary: Ubuntu 24.04.3 LTS and kernel 6.8.0-71-generic were observed before and after the change.

Healthy baseline boot ID 01c87a03-dbeb-4f85-a94d-30e88b180160 was captured, the safe restart was acknowledged, the new boot ID ffe53d45-3296-4249-a8a3-ad2ae51966f7 proved a restart, and cron plus the access policy recovered successfully.
